title: Ragnarök, the Twilight of the Gods
objective: After this level you can retell the Norse story of the end of the world and its rebirth.
summary: Ragnarok, the Norse end of the world: a three-year winter, monsters loose, Odin swallowed by Fenrir, Thor killed by the serpent's poison, then the earth rises again with two humans.

cards.headline: The Norse gods know how their world ends. They lose.
cards.body: Ragnarok is the end of the world of gods and men. It's told in the Voluspa, a 10th-century Icelandic poem, and retold in Snorri's 13th-century Prose Edda. Odin, Thor and Loki all have parts to play in the last act. Not all of them make it to the curtain call.

cards.headline: First, a winter that won't end
cards.body: It begins with the Fimbulwinter, the "Mighty Winter", which lasts three years. Then the monsters get loose. The great wolf Fenrir and Jormungand, the Midgard serpent, are freed. Remember Loki, bound to a rock? He escapes too, and steers Naglfar, a ship made of the nails of dead men. Norse myth does not do cozy.

cards.headline: The gods fall
cards.body: In the last battle, Fenrir swallows Odin. Thor kills the serpent, but its poison kills him. Surtr, the fire giant, leads the sons of Muspelheim across Bifrost and shatters the rainbow bridge. The sun turns black and the earth sinks into the sea. By now, it looks like the end of everything.

cards.context: It comes back up out of the sea, and a woman and a man, Lif and Lifthrasir, come out of the world-tree. Some gods survive to make a new home, and Balder, the god whose death Loki caused, comes back from the dead to join them. So the Norse end of the world isn't the end of the story. It's the start of the next one.
